findings.what: Design readiness deadlock: the design's consolidated spec change (scr_01M56E0GBWEPD25ZHEGXQYZ6XM) added R6.1, R7.1 and R8.20, design criteria of kind human, as ordinary criteria; designReadiness (design/approval.ts ~1018) requires every added criterion covered by a check of the effective version (stricter than D7 §7.5); the Verifier rightly wrote no check for human-judged criteria and deferred them to stage 4 (prerequisite), which is itself held design_pending: the design stays approved with ready_at null, stages 3 and 4 held, nothing in flight and no question naming the cause (design_due offers only open/waive/policy_off/later). Observed 03:17 UTC, stalled since 02:44.

The rerun of m6w_design (SURETY_REAL_RERUN=m6w_design at 292e11e, 06:38 UTC) was refused before any engine started: the harness's leftovers check (checks-journey.mjs leftovers/refuseLeftovers, evenIfPaused because the step resumes the project) counted stage 3 and stage 4's stage_build items (wi_01M56CC1ZRBKYD2HMNXY0G286C, wi_01M56CC1ZSESC8WJN99KVPM0KW; eligible, no run ever) as work of an earlier attempt that could be dispatched. They are held by the engine's computed design_pending blocker, which leftovers() does not read (it reads only dispatch_hold and the chain limit), so its own stated rule ('an eligible item not held') is not what it checks. Their release is the design step's own purpose. A harness defect of the M6 lane; no tokens spent.

After the rerun of m6w_design passed (07:00 UTC), judge (c) halted the run: 'the combined approval is in the per-act record'. recordActs on a rerun reads storeActs from the rerun's own start (sinceSeq = maxSeq at the rerun, step-starts.json overwritten to 06:56:45) and replaces the step's acts, so the first attempt's acts of the same step (design_due open 02:18, correction approvals, finding dispositions, designer_feedback, preview_inspection 02:38, combined_approval 02:39, all in the store and in driver-acts.jsonl) are absent from acts-M519.json; only qualify_adapter and preview_inspection of the rerun are recorded. A harness defect of the M6 lane's rerun; no tokens spent by it.

Confirming the review's design_verdicts (3 labs, deltas) filed 23 findings (one per implementation delta and lab), each linked to criterion R8.19 and check design-asset-favicon, whatever the delta concerns (the start-up card, input-error wording, the Run button label, the scene grid, the skip link, scene markers, a hint). Their finding_disposition 'fix' would hold the gates only until design-asset-favicon passes, a check unrelated to the defect that already passes, so a fix would be resolved by unrelated evidence; correct_check would name the same unrelated check. Also the design-kind recommendations marked 'both' were filed as implementation defects. The driver answered accept on all 23 (recorded, no gate hold); the defects stay recorded for a later run.

At most: each run (a session is one run) is bounded by 2000000 billable tokens, each Designer session by 3000000; the project's day limit of 50 USD in estimates stops it earlier (a UTC day), and its day bound on unknown usage is 4000000 tokens. The widenings are yours to confirm (policy_widening). The only hard maximum is your subscription's own usage limits.
An estimate, not a cap and not an authorization. Nothing paid starts before your qualification_approval and trust_activation.

deltas.owner_words: The Alpha's header shows the placeholder logo (PLACEHOLDER (on_dark), digest 6a8c47e8…), not the approved logo@2 on_dark (digest 1b0c17ab…). This is not a defect of this candidate: it was deployed at 13:24 UTC, before the logo was approved at 15:00, and the placeholder was correct then. Main already holds the approved on_dark logo in public/assets/logo.svg (commit 53efa50), byte-identical to the design's on_dark.svg. The difference goes away when an Alpha is deployed from main. Nothing to change in the design or the code; only a redeploy is needed. The approved logo's 3:1 viewBox fits the page's 108x36 slot unchanged.

The design's favicon slot (default variant, still the engine placeholder) is not on the page. index.html has no rel=icon link, and /favicon.svg answers 404. Change: serve design/assets/favicon/default.svg as public/favicon.svg and link it from index.html with rel=icon type=image/svg+xml. No specification criterion names the favicon, so this breaks none.

From reading app.mjs, not from use: the design says focus stays on a row's Watered button while it logs. When the button is pressed, the code rebuilds the whole list and disables the new button, so keyboard focus drops to the page body until the request ends. It then comes back to the button. Change: keep the row's button element in place while it logs (mark it aria-disabled and ignore presses rather than disabling and replacing it), so focus never leaves it.

From reading app.mjs, not from use: the design announces 'Logged a watering for <name>.' in a polite live region above the list. The code creates a new live-region element, already holding the text, on every render. Screen readers often do not announce a live region that arrives with its text already in it, so the confirmation may go unheard. The text itself is right. Change: keep one status element in the page and change only its text.
